value.assumption_check: THREE. (1) That teeth_printed (cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py:112) is the one rule for 'which teeth printed' and both the notary and the sieve already read it: measured — tester/device.py:220 _teeth calls it; the coverage sieve reads the same tool. So 'names a tooth' has one meaning. (2) That the 8 __main__-less proofs run at all under the tester: they are sealed green today because runpy.run_path with run_name __main__ executes module level and exits 0 — they exit 0 having run NOTHING that prints a tooth; the assumption is that each has functions a main() can call (measured: all 8 define test_* functions; cc/test_cc_device imports pytest and needs its teeth called directly). (3) That resealing 31 proofs is affordable: the netns seal of test_hollow took ~230s and ground_loop's beat proof 1800s; the 31 are mostly small (tools/base, build_inspector) — the reseal runs in the background in batches and its wall time is recorded on the verdict, not assumed.
value.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs, and the ticket answers: WHERE does the tester change go? cairn/devices/tester/device.py run_proof, right after `verdict = GREEN if proc.returncode == 0 else RED` (:494): if verdict is GREEN and _teeth(proc.stdout)['teeth_green'] is empty, verdict = RED and evidence.stderr_tail gets 'zero teeth printed: a green seal names at least one tooth' appended (no ninth evidence field, no new record field — the eight are ratified). WHAT counts as a tooth? Whatever teeth_printed returns green — the existing rule, unchanged. WHERE does the sieve go? cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, a function `green_seal_names_a_tooth(row, comp_dir)` beside component_color (:2937), registered in SIEVES (:3458); it walks comp_dir/validations/*.json, and for each record with verdict green whose evidence.teeth_green is missing or empty returns _finding('green_seal_names_a_tooth', component, 'a green seal names at least one tooth', expected='>= 1', actual=0, compare='gte', proof=<path>). HOW is the corpus fixed? For each of the 31: run the proof bare and read its stdout; if it prints teeth already, reseal (the seal predates the teeth convention); if not, add `if __name__ == '__main__':` that calls every test_* in the module in a try/except, prints 'PASS <name>' / 'FAIL <name>: <exc>' per tooth, and exits 1 if any failed (the shape cairn/machines/rehearsal/proofs/test_rehearsal.py main() uses); never delete or weaken a tooth; then reseal under netns through TesterDevice().run_proof(sink='validations'). cc/test_cc_device imports pytest: call its functions directly, the pytest import stays only if the venv has it (measure), else it is removed with the tooth kept. HOW is it measured done? scratchpad measure_teeth.py's count, berthed as a proof tooth in the build_inspector proof that walks the live corpus and asserts the invariant (zero), never a snapshot; plus the verdict artifact. WHAT NOT to touch: proof_coverage.py, hollow.py, clearance.py, the eight-field validation shape.
value.collision_check: Over the whys. Tester charter falsifier clause (1) 'run_proof on a passing proof yields anything but green' — its why is the notary must not lie; a proof that exits 0 and names no tooth is not 'passing', it is unmeasured, so this ADDS a clause rather than colliding: the charter delta at build says so. feeb4c786b14 (coverage declared at PROVEME) — agrees, it reads teeth_green and is blind to an empty one on a standing seal; distinction: that gate fires at a crossing, this one at every seal and over every standing seal. c5b6b128a376 (import-bound proofs red at PROVEME) — sibling, same direction. Law 7 — the tester refuses a green, collapses nothing. 'A deterministic red is fixed or carries a decision' — the 31 new reds are each fixed in the proof (D3), none plastered. No exclusive-and-terminal collision.
value.falsifier_check: DONE when (1) cairn/devices/tester/proofs/ has a tooth: TesterDevice().run_proof under a temp root on a fixture proof that exits 0 and prints no tooth name records verdict red with evidence.stderr_tail or a detail naming 'zero teeth printed', and on a fixture that prints one green tooth records green — sealed under netns; (2) cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/ has a tooth: the sieve over a fixture component whose validations hold a green record with teeth_green [] (and one with the key absent) returns one finding each in the _finding shape (about, expected, actual, compare), and over a green record naming a tooth returns none; the live assembly lists the sieve by name and phase_of derives it record; (3) the corpus census (green seals whose evidence names no tooth) reads 0 of N over cairn/**/validations, today 31 of 224, with every one of the 31 resealed green through the tester after its proof was given a runner that prints the tooth names, and no exemption list, allowlist, or skip anywhere in the tester or the sieve. RED if any green seal in the corpus names no tooth after the build, or if the tester can be made to say green over an empty teeth list by any argument. WRONG INTENT if a class of proof exists that legitimately cannot name a tooth (Akien's call, opened as a question) — the fix would still be a name, never an exemption.
value.missing_check: ONE point not wrapped, on purpose: the sieve's BAND. Akien said 'this new sieve would be in post i think'; today the band is derived by import_sieve.phase_of from what a sieve reads, and a sieve that reads a validation file derives RECORD; postprocess needs the shake to hand it the stamps, which is the shake ticket (the-shake-hands-postprocess-the-stamps, tier 3). So this cast lands the sieve as record and the shake ticket moves it; decision line D5 records that and names the follow-on. Everything else is a decision line.

value.better_approach: Considered making the proof_coverage sieve at PROVEME (feeb4c786b14) demand a non-empty teeth list instead of touching the tester. It only fires at a crossing, so 31 standing seals would stay green forever; the notary is the one place every seal passes, and the inspector sieve is the one place every STANDING seal is read. Both are needed; this is the smaller shape that covers the corpus, not just new crossings.
value.hidden_assumption: That every honest proof prints its teeth through the one convention cairn.tools.proof_coverage.teeth_printed reads. A proof using a different marker would red under this rule and be 'fixed' by adopting the convention — that is the intended pressure, but it assumes the convention is the one mouth. Also assumes the tester's own timeout path (teeth_green == [], already red) and this path never disagree — they agree by construction since both land RED.
value.prior_art: Consulted the congruency lab: the tester charter's falsifier (9 clauses) says the notary must not lie but has no clause about a green that names nothing; feeb4c786b14 (coverage declared) reads teeth_green to judge a PROVEME crossing; hollow.py:524 reads teeth_green to compare; c5b6b128a376 reds UNRAN teeth at PROVEME. None reds an EMPTY teeth list on a standing green seal — measured 31 of 209 today, so the gap is real, not narrated. The finding shape he asked about (sieve name, expected, actual, pass/fail) already exists at build_inspector/inspector.py:94 _finding — no new shape.
value.real_collision: Law 7 says a record of truth never collapses an error; the change makes the tester REFUSE a green rather than collapse anything, so no collision. Possible chafe with 'a deterministic red is fixed or carries a decision': turning 31 greens red at once is 31 deterministic reds, and D2 says each is fixed in the proof — none carries a decision, none is plastered. Distinction to record: this reds the SEAL (the notary's claim), not the proof's exit code; the proof still exits 0, the tester just declines to call that green.
